name: Stratum MagRail Platform Crew Day Rig
description:
A head-to-toe transit authority uniform built for platform-level work on the MagRail corridors. The jacket is heavyweight navy synth-canvas with a mandarin collar, Stratum Logistics embroidered chest patch in silver thread, and two diagonal hi-vis orange shoulder panels that run from collar to sleeve seam. A rear vent runs the full length of the jacket's center back, designed to accommodate basic spinal-rig augmentation with a magnetic snap closure that can be released one-handed. The trousers are charcoal stretch-twill with reinforced knee panels, two deep cargo pockets with velcro-tab closures, and a built-in tool loop belt sewn into the waistband. A retractable badge lanyard clips to a D-ring at the left chest. Underfoot: steel-toe flatform boots in matte black synth-leather with orange reflective piping along the heel and ankle, oil-resistant soles rated for wet platform surfaces.

The worker's name patch — white embroidery on black — sits above the right breast pocket. A thin thermal base layer in Stratum gray shows at the collar. A matte-black transit authority helmet with folding visor hangs from a carabiner at the hip when not worn. Gloves — cut-resistant synth-leather with open fingertips for BCI touchpad operation — are tucked into the left cargo pocket. The whole rig reads as institutional and maintained: pressed but not pristine, bearing the scuff marks of daily platform life.
functionality: Spinal-rig vent with magnetic closure, tool loop waistband, D-ring badge attachment, reinforced knee panels, oil-resistant steel-toe boots, BCI-compatible open-fingertip gloves, retractable lanyard, deep cargo pockets
what_it_says: This is someone employed by a major corponation transit system — not a contractor, an actual employee with benefits and a union card. The pressed name patch and intact branding say they take pride in the work even if the work is grinding. The aug-vent on the jacket back suggests they've got a spinal rig — probably for platform hazard alerts or load-monitoring. Reliable, institutional, tired in a dignified way.
worn_by: ticketing booth workers on outdoor platforms
manufacturer: Stratum Logistics — corponation-issued uniform, minor field repairs by wearer
price_range: Φ 180–Φ 240 (corponation-issued; replacement cost to worker if lost)
story_hooks: A platform worker's Stratum name patch belongs to someone who died six months ago — the current wearer acquired it through channels they won't explain, and now Stratum's HR enforcement unit is looking for the discrepancy.
The magnetic spinal-rig vent has been modified to conceal a data-chip smuggling channel — someone is moving sensitive route data out of the MagRail network one shift at a time.

A player character needs to move through a restricted transit zone undetected; acquiring and wearing this uniform is the most plausible cover — but every platform worker knows every other platform worker by face.

physical_description.visual_profile: Authoritative transit worker silhouette — structured, safety-forward, built for repetitive physical labor in electromagnetic corridors. The navy jacket dominates with bold orange hi-vis accents that read as institutional authority. Chunky steel-toe boots ground the figure. Overall impression: working-class competence, corpo-regulated, visible rank.
physical_description.fit: Tailored through the shoulders and chest for mobility and augmentation accommodation, relaxed through the torso to allow layering and tool access. Trousers are straight-leg with mild taper at the ankle, fitted enough to prevent catching on machinery but loose enough for crouching and ladder work.
physical_description.primary_material: Heavyweight navy synth-canvas jacket (ballistic-grade weave); charcoal stretch-twill trousers with reinforced nylon knee panels; matte black synth-leather boots with oil-resistant polymer sole; gray thermal base layer (synthetic wool blend)
physical_description.texture: Canvas has a crisp, woven surface with subtle ribbing; trousers show a fine twill weave with slight stretch sheen; boots are matte-finished with tactile grip-tread; embroidered patches create raised texture focal points
physical_description.color_scheme: Primary navy blue jacket with charcoal gray trousers and matte black boots. Safety-critical orange hi-vis shoulder panels and reflective heel/ankle piping. Silver-thread embroidery (Stratum Logistics patch, name tag). Stratum gray thermal layer visible at collar.
physical_description.closures: Jacket: full-length coil zipper with magnetic snap rear vent for spinal-rig access; trousers: standard waistband with belt loops and two velcro-tab cargo pockets; boots: full lace-up with metal eyelets; helmet: carabiner clip at hip
distinctive_features: Diagonal hi-vis orange shoulder panels (emergency visibility)
Embroidered Stratum Logistics chest patch in silver thread
White embroidered name patch above right breast pocket
D-ring for retractable badge lanyard at left chest
Integrated tool loop belt sewn into waistband
Folding-visor transit helmet with carabiner attachment
Reflective piping on boots (wet platform safety)
Cut-resistant synth-leather fingerless gloves in left cargo pocket
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3 — working-class corpo issue. Functional, durable, standardized. Not luxury, but well-maintained institutional gear. The presence of integrated augmentation accommodation signals mid-tier infrastructure workers.
physical_description.cultural_context: This rig marks the wearer as essential transit infrastructure staff — platform-level MagRail crews. Wearing it signals allegiance to a mega-logistics corporation, compliance with safety protocols, and likely some form of neural interface for train coordination. It's neither street nor elite; it's the uniform of the organized working class that keeps the GLMZ moving.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pressed and maintained, but visibly worn. Scuffs on the boots from platform grating; faint grease stains on the cargo pockets (tool residue); the jacket's canvas shows subtle creases from repeated movement; name patch may show minor fraying at edges. This is an outfit that's respected but lived-in.
